title: Felix and the Inheritance
premise: Insurance investigator Casper Okonkwo receives two anonymous letters about the drowning of Marguerite Voss ten years ago: one confessing to murder, the other promising a fortune for his silence. As he reopens the case everyone in Hollowmere swore was closed, his photographic memory becomes both weapon and curse, forcing him to confront the found family at the Voss estate who raised him after his parents' death. The killer is Marguerite's devoted housekeeper, Agnes, who drowned her to protect the twins from their mother's plan to disinherit them and flee with the estate; the second letter came from Agnes herself, dying of cancer, wanting absolution before the anniversary dinner. At the dinner, Casper must choose between exposing her and preserving the only family he has ever had, ultimately revealing the truth privately and letting Agnes die free while the town keeps its comfortable lie.
about_author: Sable Eriksen is the pen name of a former claims adjuster from coastal Maine who spent fifteen years reading other people's disasters for a living. Their debut novels are known for quiet towns hiding loud secrets and investigators who remember everything except how to let go.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Casper Okonkwo files claims by day and alphabetizes the town's secrets by night until two letters arrive in the same envelope: one confessing to Marguerite Voss's murder, one offering money for silence. His hands shake as he reads them twice, memorizing every word against his will. POV: Casper. Beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Invitations arrive for the tenth-anniversary memorial dinner at Voss House, hosted by the twins, Delphine and Marcus. Casper realizes whoever sent the letters wants the case reopened—or buried—before that night. He burns neither letter. POV: Casper. Beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: A Town That Forgets on Purpose
chapters.summary: Casper walks Hollowmere's main street, cataloguing what everyone pretends not to know: the closed boathouse, the repainted dock, the constable who retired early. Flashbacks show him arriving orphaned at fourteen, taken in by the Voss household. POV: Casper. Beat: loneliness beneath belonging.

chapters.title: Agnes Still Makes the Bread
chapters.summary: Casper visits Voss House under pretext of updating the estate's insurance. Agnes Whitlock, the housekeeper who helped raise him, feeds him like family and asks nothing. He watches her hands and wonders if they could have held a woman underwater. POV: Casper. Beat: love complicating suspicion.

chapters.title: Delphine's Ledger
chapters.summary: Delphine Voss, now running the family shipping business, is crisp and defensive when Casper asks about the estate's finances. He notices a ledger page torn out—dated the week of the drowning. She notices him noticing. POV: Casper. Beat: first open hostility.

chapters.title: What Marcus Drowned In
chapters.summary: Marcus Voss, the charming twin, drinks too much at the harbor tavern and nearly tells Casper something before his wife pulls him away. Casper memorizes the sentence Marcus never finished: 'She was going to take us off the—' POV: Casper. Beat: the confession has a shape now.

chapters.title: File 10-V-114
chapters.summary: In the archive basement, Casper pulls the original file: accidental drowning, no autopsy, signed off by Constable Hale. His memory flags an inconsistency—the tide chart doesn't match where the body was found. POV: Casper. Beat: the professional thrill of a real anomaly.

chapters.title: The Confession Reread
chapters.summary: Alone, Casper recites the confession letter from memory and finds its flaw: it describes details only someone present could know, but gets the weather wrong. Either the writer lied deliberately or remembers wrongly. Both possibilities terrify him. POV: Casper. Beat: the letter is bait, not truth.

chapters.title: Constable Hale's Quiet Years
chapters.summary: Casper visits retired Constable Hale, now growing tomatoes and avoiding eye contact. Hale admits he was told to close the file by Marguerite's lawyer, Silas Crane. 'Some drownings are kinder than accidents,' Hale says, and shuts the door. POV: Casper. Beat: complicity everywhere.

chapters.title: Silas Crane's Fee
chapters.summary: Lawyer Silas Crane receives Casper in an office smelling of pipe smoke and warns him off with polite menace, hinting the twins' inheritance depends on the verdict staying 'accident.' Casper realizes Crane drafted both wills—the old one and the new. POV: Casper. Beat: money as motive, but whose?

chapters.title: Agnes's Garden
chapters.summary: A tender chapter: Agnes and Casper garden together as they did when he was a boy. She mentions Marguerite only once, softly, calling her 'a woman at war with herself.' Casper leaves more unsettled than any interrogation has made him. POV: Casper. Beat: the suspect he loves most.

chapters.title: The Second Letter's Sender
chapters.summary: Casper traces the stationery of the money-for-silence letter to the village shop; only three people buy it. Surveillance of his own habits reveals he's being watched back—a figure outside his cottage at night. POV: Casper. Beat: hunter becoming hunted.

chapters.title: Delphine Follows Him
chapters.summary: Confronted, Delphine admits she hired someone to watch Casper after the letters arrived—she received one too. Hers promised the truth would surface at the dinner unless she paid. Someone is extorting the whole household. POV: Casper. Beat: alliance forming across suspicion.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Plan
chapters.summary: Digging into the missing ledger page through shipping records, Casper reconstructs Marguerite's final weeks: she was liquidating assets, booking passage abroad, planning to remarry and cut the twins out entirely. The 'loving mother' was abandoning her children. POV: Casper. Beat: the victim stops being innocent.

chapters.title: Marcus Breaks
chapters.summary: Drunk and terrified by the extortion letter, Marcus begs Casper to make it stop, babbling that he saw someone on the dock that night and has pretended for ten years not to know who. He passes out before naming them. POV: Casper. Beat: the witness who chose blindness.

chapters.title: The Boathouse
chapters.summary: Casper searches the sealed boathouse and finds a hidden cache: Marguerite's real will, leaving everything to a foundation—and a train ticket dated the day after she died. She never intended to stay. Neither, perhaps, did her killer intend anything at all. POV: Casper. Beat: evidence that reframes everything.

chapters.title: Someone Searches His Cottage
chapters.summary: Returning home, Casper finds his cottage searched with surgical care—nothing stolen, everything read. Only one person knew his filing system well enough to search it so cleanly. He sits in the dark, unable to say the name. POV: Casper. Beat: betrayal narrowing to a face.

chapters.title: Hale Comes to Him
chapters.summary: Constable Hale, rattled by Casper's questions reaching others, visits at night and half-confesses: he suspected foul play, was paid to look away, and has hated himself for a decade. He gives Casper the name scratched from the visitor log that week. It's illegible—but the handwriting isn't. POV: Casper. Beat: guilt seeking company.

chapters.title: Crane's Mistake
chapters.summary: Casper baits Silas Crane with a fake claim that the original will has surfaced. Crane's panicked response reveals he knew about the real will all along—he helped hide it, for a fee, from someone. The fee matches the amount in the silence letter. POV: Casper. Beat: the extortionist and the hider may be one.

chapters.title: Anniversary Preparations
chapters.summary: Voss House fills with flowers, caterers, and returning guests. Agnes works herself ragged directing everything, and Casper sees her collapse briefly in the pantry, gray-faced. She waves off help. There is less time than anyone knows. POV: Casper. Beat: tenderness and countdown entwined.

chapters.title: The Third Letter
chapters.summary: A third letter arrives, addressed in a hand Casper finally recognizes: Agnes's. It contains no confession and no threat—only the words 'Tell them at dinner, or I will.' The blackmailer is the confessor. The mystery collapses into a single grieving person. POV: Casper. Beat: devastating recognition.

chapters.title: Why She Wrote
chapters.summary: Casper confronts Agnes gently. Dying of cancer, she couldn't bear the lie another year, but couldn't destroy the twins either—so she split her conscience into two letters, hoping fate or Casper would decide. She asks him: 'What does a debt cost when the creditor is dead?' POV: Casper. Beat: the killer as the kindest person he knows.

chapters.title: That Night on the Dock
chapters.summary: Agnes tells the full story: she followed Marguerite to the dock, meant only to beg her to stay for the twins, and when Marguerite mocked her devotion and threatened to take even Agnes's found family apart, they struggled. The water did the rest. She has filed it under survival ever since. POV: Casper (listening). Beat: horror braided with heartbreak.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Casper walks the coast all night, weighing themes against each other: the law, the twins' futures, his own debt to Agnes, Marguerite's cruelty. His memory replays every kindness she ever showed him against the drowned woman's sneer. He cannot make the columns balance. POV: Casper. Beat: moral paralysis at the midpoint's far side.

chapters.title: Delphine Suspects
chapters.summary: Delphine, sharp as her mother, corners Casper: she's found the real will's absence noted in Crane's files and demands to know what he knows. Lying to her feels like lying to family—which, he realizes, is exactly what he'd be doing. POV: Casper. Beat: loyalty splitting down the middle.

chapters.title: Marcus Remembers
chapters.summary: Sober for the first time in years, Marcus tells Casper what he truly saw: Agnes on the dock, and Marguerite's hand striking her face first. He stayed silent because Agnes was the only parent who ever actually parented him. His silence was gratitude. POV: Casper. Beat: the whole family is guilty of love.

chapters.title: Crane Escalates
chapters.summary: Silas Crane, realizing Casper has assembled the picture, threatens to expose everything himself unless the estate pays him off—turning protector of the secret into its auctioneer. Casper photographs Crane's own blackmail letter with a steady hand. POV: Casper. Beat: a new enemy made from an old accomplice.

chapters.title: The Archive Fire
chapters.summary: A fire guts the records office; the original drowning file burns. Arson, obviously—Crane covering tracks, or someone else entirely. Casper's memory is now the only copy of the evidence that exists, making him the case. POV: Casper. Beat: the investigator becomes the archive.

chapters.title: What Casper Owes
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Casper's first months at Voss House, Agnes teaching him that memory is a gift only if you choose what to do with it. 'You don't have to remember out loud,' she told him. Now her own words return as either absolution or indictment. POV: Casper. Beat: the past arming the present.

chapters.title: Delphine Finds Out
chapters.summary: Delphine pieces it together independently—she is her mother's daughter—and comes to Casper white-faced, asking not whether Agnes did it, but whether exposing her will save or destroy what's left of them. Two keepers of the secret, deciding together. POV: Casper. Beat: complicity offered as intimacy.

chapters.title: Crane's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Crane sets a deadline: payment before the dinner, or he goes public with a version of events that ruins the twins and spares himself. Casper realizes stopping Crane matters as much as deciding about Agnes. He begins building a trap out of paperwork. POV: Casper. Beat: the investigator investigates again.

chapters.title: The Trap Is Set
chapters.summary: Casper feeds Crane forged proof that the real will incriminates Crane directly. Greedy and frightened, Crane takes the bait to a midnight meeting at the boathouse—where Constable Hale, come to make amends, waits with a constable's badge and a recorder. POV: Casper. Beat: justice via the town's own machinery.

chapters.title: Crane Falls
chapters.summary: Crane is arrested for blackmail, tampering, and obstruction; his confession drags Hale's old bribe into daylight too. The town's scaffolding of lies cracks publicly, but the central secret—Agnes—holds, unspoken. Casper watches the twins absorb the scandal. POV: Casper. Beat: partial justice, full cost.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: On the eve of the dinner, Casper and Agnes sit in the kitchen like old times. She knows tomorrow may end her; he knows he holds the knife. They bake bread together and say everything without saying it. POV: Casper. Beat: the calmest, saddest chapter.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Voss House glitters; glasses rise to Marguerite's memory. Delphine gives a speech that is technically true and emotionally false. Under the chandelier, Agnes catches Casper's eye across the room—a question, a permission, a farewell. POV: Casper. Beat: the held breath of the whole book.

chapters.title: Casper Speaks
chapters.summary: Asked to say a few words, Casper stands and—instead of the safe toast—tells the room a version of the truth: that Marguerite was leaving them, that someone loved this family enough to commit a terrible sin to protect it, and that forgiveness is owed to the living. He never names Agnes. The room understands anyway. POV: Casper. Beat: climax—truth as mercy, delivered publicly, precisely.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Pantry
chapters.summary: Guests leave in murmuring clusters. In the pantry, Agnes thanks Casper with bread and tears; Delphine embraces them both, choosing family over verdict. Marcus weeps with relief. The secret is now shared, which means it is finally carried instead of hidden. POV: Casper. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Agnes's Last Season
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Agnes declines quickly but peacefully, tended by the three people she saved and damned. She dies in the garden with Casper holding her hand, whispering that she'd do it again, and that she's sorry, and that he was the best thing she ever grew. POV: Casper. Beat: grief earned honestly.

chapters.title: Filing the Case
chapters.summary: Casper writes the official report—accidental drowning, case closed—and files it beside the burned original, then writes a private account for the twins alone, the true record preserved where it can do no public harm. Some truths belong to families, not archives. POV: Casper. Beat: resolution of the investigator's code.

chapters.title: What Casper Keeps
chapters.summary: One year on: Casper stays in Hollowmere, no longer invisible but chosen. Delphine runs the business with the foundation's new purpose; Marcus is sober; the town slowly forgives itself. On the anniversary, Casper bakes Agnes's bread recipe badly and lets the smoke alarm scream—alive, remembered, home. POV: Casper. Beat: found family, kept.
